# Pulsar OS

> Pulsar OS is a family of free, open-source Linux operating systems ("flavours")
> designed to be easy: each flavour copies the look and workflow of an operating
> system people already use (macOS, Windows, TV), so switching to Linux requires
> no relearning. It combines that ease of use with the total freedom only Linux
> gives. Pulsar OS is not a theme or a repackaged desktop: it ports the whole
> workflow of each system and builds new native tools for it — session restore
> (choose "save session" on shutdown and the session comes back exactly as it
> was), the Sayri local AI assistant (connect any AI provider, works fully with
> local models, sandboxed like OpenClaw but secure), macOS-style window
> management, Time Machine backups (network server, 50 cloud providers or USB,
> restorable from recovery), Circle to Search (search on Google, ask Sayri or
> OCR any part of the screen) and a universal app store that
> bridges apt, pacman, AUR and Flathub. It is a complete operating system
> designed around user comfort, unlike distributions that only ship a theme or
> package an existing desktop. All code and builds are public on GitHub.

Pulsar OS is developed by the Inled community (Spain). The flavours are
independent editions: each one has its own website, its own ISO and its own
focus. This site is the umbrella project: it lists the flavours, hosts the
community space and the documentation.

## What makes it different

- Full workflow ports, not cosmetic themes: window management, gestures and
  desktop flow are rebuilt per flavour.
- Session restore: windows and apps come back exactly as they were after
  shutdown or power loss (see
  [hibernation and session restore](https://os.inled.es/help/hardware/hibernation-and-session-restore)).
- Sayri: a local-first AI assistant integrated into the desktop, with skills,
  gateways and sandboxed execution (see
  [Sayri architecture](https://os.inled.es/help/architecture/sayri)).
- Pulsar Store: one app store bridging Flatpak, GNOME Extensions, apt, pacman
  and AUR (see [store architecture](https://os.inled.es/help/architecture/store)).

## Flavours

- [Bitten Fruit](https://bittenfruit.inled.es): The published flavour. Easy
  Linux for Mac users: a macOS-style desktop (top bar, dock, gestures, session
  restore, Finder-style file manager, Spotlight search, Sayri AI assistant, and
  an app store that bridges apt, pacman, AUR and Flathub) with the total freedom
  of Linux. Available in Debian and Arch editions, with GRUB or rEFInd boot.
- Wintux (in development): A Windows-style desktop edition.
- Tube OS (in development): A living-room / NAS edition for TV and home server
  use, based on CasaOS and Plasma Bigscreen.

## Main pages

- [Home](https://os.inled.es/index): Overview of the project and its flavours.
- [Bitten Fruit (flavour page)](https://bittenfruit.inled.es): The
  macOS-style edition: features, editions, downloads.
- [New to Linux](https://os.inled.es/new-to-linux): Explainer for switchers
  from macOS or Windows: what changes under the hood, in plain language, and a
  short guide to using Pulsar OS (apps, updates, files, keyboard, recovery).
- [Community](https://os.inled.es/community): Reported errors, ideas, community
  tasks, suggestions and the project roadmap.
- [Help & Documentation](https://os.inled.es/help): Install guides, usage
  documentation, hardware notes and contributing docs.
- [Downloads](https://downloads-os.inled.es): Downloads and install guides for the
  editions.
- [Resources](https://os.inled.es/resources): Logos, banners and media assets.

## For developers

- Code is fully public and auditable; ISOs are built with GitHub Actions.
- Contributions from beginners are welcome, including non-code work
  (docs, translations, design, testing). AI-assisted contributions are allowed
  if tested before submitting; see
  [the AI policy](https://os.inled.es/help/contributing/use-ai).
- Developer setup guide:
  [developer setup](https://os.inled.es/help/contributing/developer-setup).
